It is recorded by a magistrate
Remains valid even after the recovery of the depositor

question: A 36-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a fever lasting for three days, accompanied by mild abdominal pain. Fastest molecular test for TB?

A 36-year-old man from Larkhana who works as a labourer came in with a 6-week-old, painless ulcer on his right forearm. The edges had stiff margins, and a raised crust was present in the centre. Additionally, according to her mother, her daughter also got a rash that started on her face and then moved to her lower limbs, including her palms and soles. A 5-year-old youngster was brought to the outpatient department complaining of water-filled blisters over his trunk, upper and lower extremities, and entire body. He also reported having a fever, malaise, and intense itching. Based on clinical evidence, the doctor suspected that he had varicella. Additionally, she experienced a three-day-long rash that began on her face and spread to her trunk and extremities. Antibody titer increases fourfold in serologic diagnosis. A 35-year-old guy arrived at the emergency room complaining of a fever, malaise, and cough along with excruciating joint and muscular discomfort. Leucopenia and thrombocytopenia are shown on his CBC report. The results of the serological test revealed NS1 antigen positivity. A 35-year-old man came in complaining of discomfort, edema, and pruritus in his ears and distal extremities for the previous 1.5 years. Physical investigations showed bilateral eyelash loss, nonpitting edema of the ears, and ill-defined, somewhat dusky, hyperpigmented patches distributed symmetrically and diffusely across his limbs, sparing the neck and torso.
